newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Joe White lowers full year forecast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Joe White lowers full year forecast.

text.p: Malting group Joe White Maltings Ltd said on Tuesday it was now projecting a lower profit for the 1996/97 year (July-June) than that contained in the Grant Samuel report issued last year during the failed takeover bid by stockfeed group Ridley Corp Ltd.

"The board is projecting for the year to June 30, 1997, a profit below the forecast contained in the Grant Samuel report dated September 17, 1996," Joe White Maltings said in its interim profit statements.
The Grant Samuel report forecast a rise in net profits for 1996/97 to A$9.8 million from A$6.81 million in 1995/96.
Joe White said the changes were mainly due to the deferment of the likely sailing date for certain bulk shipments which would be picked up in the following period.
There were also some potential cuts in expected contractual tonnages and a drop in by-products income because of a a fall in feed prices, it said.
"The projected trading profit is still expected to be a record for the company," it said.
Joe White said it still expected to see a fall in profits in the 1997/98 year.
"This will be directly due to to the misguided conduct of a few European maltsters," the company said.
"They spoiled for themselves and everyone else a promising world market."
"The board continue to consider this an aberration and believes that the 1998/99 profit will resume its upward path," it said.
Joe White did not explain the "misguided conduct" but said on November 12, in forecasting a lower 1997/98 profit, that malt prices had been driven down in Europe.
Earlier Joe White reported a first half net profit of A$3.97 million, up from A$3.04 million a year earlier. This included an abnormal loss of A$1.23 million.
It raised its interim dividend to 11 cents per share from nine cents per share.
Joe White's shares closed unchanged at A$4.90.
